channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Canada’s Loblaw misses fourth-quarter revenue estimates
item.description: Canadian retailer Loblaw on Wednesday missed analysts’ estimates for fourth-quarter revenue, signaling consumers are turning cautious and more discerning in their spending pattern as tariff uncertainty hovers.

item.title: U.S., Canada to meet in coming weeks on trade, Greer says
item.description: U.S. and Canadian trade officials spoke on Wednesday and plan to meet in coming weeks, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said, adding that the Trump administration was open to their ideas on how to reach an agreement.

item.title: Protein Industries Canada funds nine food processing projects across Canada
item.description: Nine food processing companies across Canada are set to see projects funded by Protein Industries Canada.

item.title: Saskatchewan premier heads to India for trade talks
item.description: Saskatchewan premier Scott Moe said a trade mission to India will focus on agriculture, potash and uranium as the province seeks trade opportunities and solid trading relationships in that market.

item.title: Feed costs on rented pasture now eligible for AgriStability
item.description: Pasture-related feed costs are now allowable expenses for AgriStability participants.

item.title: Incoming Canadian Cattle Association CEO embraces winds of change
item.description: Andrea Brocklebank, the incoming CEO of the Canadian Cattle Association, is open to revitalizing the organization while maintaining national delivery.

item.title: CBOT Weekly: Several unknowns that could affect commodity prices
item.description: There are a number of unknowns that could affect where soy, corn and wheat prices go on the Chicago Board of Trade, said Sean Lusk, vice-president of Walsh Commercial Hedging Services.

item.title: Bayer’s proposed Roundup settlement faces first signs of pushback in court
item.description: Law firms representing nearly 20,000 people who sued Bayer over alleged injuries from its Roundup weedkiller urged a Missouri judge to delay reviewing the German company’s proposed US$7.25 billion nationwide settlement, arguing that rushing would violate the rights of cancer patients and their families.
